function: Joint learned control of BS beamforming, UAV-mounted RIS phase shifts and UAV trajectory, maximizing minimum secrecy energy efficiency under imperfect CSI and phase errors (pp. 3, 6)
system: BS with 4 antennas, 2 single-antenna users, 1 eavesdropper; reflecting RIS (UPA, 16-64 elements) on a UAV; 28 GHz (pp. 3, 9, 11)
method: Twin-TD3 deep reinforcement learning (IA-CSORL): agent 1 sets beamforming and RIS phases with PRAD optimizer, agent 2 sets UAV trajectory with ESIA attention (pp. 6-10)
data_channel: Own simulator: 3D Saleh-Valenzuela model with Rician factors, path-loss exponents 2.2 and 3.5, imperfect CSI factor 0.1, von Mises phase errors; no standard channel (pp. 4-5, 11)
test_conditions: Same scenario for training and evaluation (2 moving users); sweeps of RIS elements 16-64, phase-error scale 0.1-1.5, GPS error 3 m; no unseen scenario (pp. 10-13)
baselines: Learned only: TDDRL [40] (single TD3), TTD3 [26] (twin-agent TD3), and ablations TTD3 with PRAD only or ESIA only; no non-learned baseline (p. 11)
metrics: Average reward convergence, sum secrecy rate (SSR), secrecy energy efficiency (SEE), UAV trajectories (pp. 11-13)
complexity: Order of inference complexity O(Ds Da + Da^2 + sum Nl Nl+1) per step, versus O(Iiter M^3.5) for iterative solvers, analytical only (p. 10)
q1_support: p. 4: "the channel follows the 3D Saleh-Valenzuela (SV) model" - custom simulator with Rician terms and own path-loss exponents (p. 11); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 12: "We further compare SSR and SEE with and without PRAD under different phase-error levels" - sweeps of phase error, RIS elements (p. 12) and GPS error (p. 13) in one fixed layout (p. 10); no model trained in one setting and tested in another.
q3_support: p. 11: "The proposed method is compared against the following baselines" - TDDRL [40], TTD3 [26] and two ablations, all learned; Figs. 4 and 6 show no non-learned baseline (SCA and SDR solvers appear only in the complexity discussion, p. 10).
q4_support: p. 10: "evaluated via floating-point operations (FLOPs), with a primary focus on the online inference phase" - order O(Ds Da + Da^2 + sum Nl Nl+1) per inference step, versus O(Iiter M^3.5) for iterative solvers.
q5_support: p. 10: "This section presents the numerical results to evaluate" the method - own simulation with parameters in Table II (p. 9); no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Included as area 6 by the specificity order: UAV-mounted RIS (aerial) link with learned beam, RIS phase and trajectory control; the above-PHY check passes because beamforming and RIS phases are learned jointly with the trajectory (pp. 3, 6). Area 3 is the alternative if a UAV-mounted RIS link is not treated as an aerial link. Title on p. 1 matches the DOI.
